translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses and Aaron with a speaking.
translations.2: Any person in whose skin of his body there was a mark, or a blemish, or a spot — or there appeared in the skin of his body an affliction of leprosy — he shall be brought to Aaron the imām, or to one of his sons the imāms.
translations.3: And the imām shall inspect the affliction in the skin of the body; if there is in it hair that has turned white, and the appearance of the affliction is deep from the skin of his body, it is an affliction of leprosy — and when it is seen thus, he shall declare him impure.
translations.4: But if the spot in the skin of his body is white, and its appearance is not deep from the skin, and its hair has not turned white, he shall confine him for seven days.
translations.5: Then he shall inspect him on the seventh day; if the affliction has stood as it was and has not spread in the skin, he shall confine him for a second seven days.
translations.6: Then he shall inspect him on the seventh day a second time; if it has dimmed and has not spread in the skin, he shall declare him pure — for it is a blemish — and he shall wash his garments and be pure.
translations.7: But if the blemish spreads in the skin after he was shown to the imām and he declared him pure, he shall be shown to him a second time.
translations.8: And if the imām sees that it has spread in his skin, he shall declare him impure — for it is leprosy.
translations.9: If there is on a person an affliction of leprosy, he shall be brought to the imām.
translations.10: And the imām shall inspect — and behold, if there is a white mark in his skin and the hair has turned white, or there is a portion of raw flesh in the mark,
translations.11: it is an old leprosy in the skin of his body; the imām shall declare him impure and shall not confine him, since he is impure.
translations.12: And if the leprosy spreads throughout the body, until it covers all the skin of the afflicted one from his head to his feet — entirely within the sight of the imām's eyes —
translations.13: the imām shall inspect; and if the leprosy has covered all his body, he shall declare him pure, since it has all turned white — he is pure.
translations.14: But on whatever day raw flesh appears in him, he shall declare him impure.
translations.15: For when the imām sees the raw flesh, he shall declare him impure — for a portion of raw flesh together with the leprosy is impure.
translations.16: But if the raw flesh turns back and becomes white, he shall come to the imām.
translations.17: And if the imām inspects and the affliction has turned white, he shall declare him pure — he is pure.
translations.18: And any person in whose skin of his body there was a sore, and it healed —
translations.19: and there appeared in its place a white mark, or a white spot tinged with red — he shall be shown to the imām.
translations.20: And if the imām sees that its appearance is sunken below the skin and its hair has turned white, he shall declare him impure — for it is an affliction of leprosy that has spread in the sore.
translations.21: But if he inspects it and there is no white hair in it, and it is not sunken below the skin but is rather dim, he shall confine him for seven days.
translations.22: And if it spreads in the skin, he shall declare him impure — for it is an affliction.
translations.23: But if it stays in its place and has not spread, it is from the trace of the sore; the imām shall declare him pure.
translations.24: Any person in whose skin there was a burn from fire, and the part of the burn became a white spot tinged with red, or white only —
translations.25: the imām shall inspect it; and if the hair has turned white and its appearance is deep from the skin, it is leprosy that has spread in the burn — the imām shall declare him impure.
translations.26: But if the imām sees that there is no white hair in it, and it is not sunken below the skin but is rather dim, he shall confine him for seven days.
translations.27: Then he shall inspect it on the seventh day; if it has spread in the skin, he shall declare him impure — for it is an affliction of leprosy.
translations.28: But if it stays in its place and has not spread in the skin, and it is dim — it is from the trace of the burn; the imām shall declare him pure, for it is a scorching of the burn.
translations.29: And any man or woman in whom there is an affliction of leprosy in the head or in the beard —
translations.30: the imām shall inspect it; and if its appearance is deep from the skin and there is in it thin yellowish hair, the imām shall declare him impure — for it is a blight, and it is leprosy of the head or the beard.
translations.31: But if it is seen, and its appearance is not deep from the skin and there is no black hair in it, he shall confine him for seven days.
translations.32: Then he shall inspect it on the seventh day — if it has not spread, and there has not appeared in it yellowish hair, and its appearance is not deep from the skin —
translations.33: he shall shave his hair, except for the place of the blight, and he shall confine him for a second seven days.
translations.34: Then he shall inspect it on the seventh day; if it has not spread in the skin, and its appearance is moreover not deep from the skin, the imām shall declare him pure; and he shall wash his garments, that he may be pure.
translations.35: But if the blight spreads in his body after his purification —
translations.36: the imām shall inspect it, and behold it has spread in the skin: he need not examine for the yellowish hair — by proof that he is impure.
translations.37: But if it has stood as it was, and black hair has grown in it, then it has healed and he is pure; the imām shall declare him pure.
translations.38: And any man or woman in whose skin of his body there are spots — spots that are white —
translations.39: the imām shall inspect; and if in the skin of their bodies the spots are dim in their whiteness, it is vitiligo that has spread in the skin — and he is pure.
translations.40: And any person whose hair has fallen out — he is the bald one, and he is pure.
translations.41: And if it has fallen out from the side of his face, he is the forehead-bald one, and he is pure.
translations.42: But if there is in the bald patch or in the forehead-bald patch a white affliction tinged with red, it may be leprosy that has spread in his bald patch or his forehead-bald patch.
translations.43: The imām shall inspect: if the mark of the affliction is white tinged with red, in his bald patch or his forehead-bald patch, after the manner of the appearances of leprosy of the rest of the skin of the body and its rulings —
translations.44: he is a leprous man and he is impure; the imām shall declare him thoroughly impure, for his affliction is in his head.
translations.45: And the leper in whom the affliction is — his garments must be torn and his head shall be disheveled, and he shall cover over his mustache, and he shall call out: 'Impure! Impure!'
translations.46: For as long as the affliction remains in him he shall be impure — for he is impure; he shall dwell alone, outside the camp shall be his dwelling-place.
translations.47: And any garment in which there is an affliction of leprosy — whether a garment of wool or
translations.48: of linen, or in warp or weft of linen or wool, or in hide, or in anything made from it —
translations.49: and the affliction is green or red, in the garment or the hide, or the warp or the weft, or in any article of hides — that is an affliction of leprosy; it shall be shown to the imām.
translations.50: When it is seen, he shall confine it for seven days.
translations.51: Then he shall inspect it on the seventh day; if the affliction has spread in the garment, or the warp or the weft, or in the hide, or in the rest of what is made from hides as a manufactured article — that is a consuming affliction of leprosy, and it is impure.
translations.52: He shall burn the garment, or the warp or the weft, whether of wool or linen, or all the articles of hides in which the affliction is — for it is a consuming leprosy; therefore it shall be burned with fire.
translations.53: But if the imām sees that it has not spread in the garment, or the warp or the weft, or in any article of hides —
translations.54: he shall command that it be washed, and he shall confine it for a second seven days.
translations.55: Then he shall inspect it after it has been washed; if its color has not changed and it has not spread, it is impure — it shall be burned with fire; it was a destructive thing, whether in its worn part or in its new part.
translations.56: But if he sees that it has dimmed after it was washed, he shall scrape it from the garment or the hide, and cut it out from the warp or the weft.
translations.57: And if it appears further in the garment, or the warp or the weft, or in any article of hides — it is the spreading one; the garment in which the affliction is shall be burned with fire.
translations.58: But the garment, or the warp or the weft, or any article of hides — if they are washed and the affliction departs from them, they shall be washed a second time and they shall be pure.
translations.59: This is the ordinance of the affliction of leprosy in a garment of wool or linen, or warp or weft, or any article of hides — to declare it pure or to declare it impure.
